answer: For pigment demand at a harbor, a forecast market can price trades from one shared cost function C(q), where q records outstanding outcome shares. An agent called falcon pays C(q+d)-C(q) for a trade d, with no signup credits or per-trade subsidies. Splitting the same sequence across aliases leaves total cost unchanged because intermediate terms cancel. Fake accounts cannot cheaply multiply influence by casting extra forecast votes. This makes identity splitting neutral, but funded manipulation remains possible and settlement needs a trustworthy demand measurement.
